ABOUT ASTERA:

Astera is a private foundation on a mission to steer science and technology toward a better future. We believe the coming years will bring an era of unprecedented scientific and technological advancement as exponential progress in AI converges with central advances in other fields to accelerate innovation. This inflection point provides an unparalleled opportunity to fundamentally rethink the institutions, systems, and tools that drive progress. We have committed a $3.5B endowment to that work and fit the form of our support to the function it serves: grants, investments, and in-house research programs. We accept meaningful risk in the research we back and expect some of it to fail because transformative ideas are rarely the ones already proven. Our projects, and the foundation itself, operate like high-velocity startups, with a high performance bar and competitive compensation to match. We are searching for leaders who are compelled by the challenge of driving high-impact change in the way science is funded, conducted, and communicated. You can read more about our mission, vision, and programming at astera.org/vision http://astera.org/vision.




PROJECT SUMMARY: 

We are building a frontier robotics lab at Astera Institute. We believe neuroscience and AI will converge in embodied intelligence: animals and robots face shared challenges of perceiving their surroundings, navigating, manipulating objects, and using memory and reasoning to accomplish tasks in the physical world. Robotics provides a powerful testbed for investigating how biological neural circuits solve these challenges and for developing AI systems that turn perception, learning, and cognition into effective action.

Our strategy starts with developing a mechanistic understanding of how neural circuits can generate intelligent behavior, and applying specific mechanism to make robots useful. We aim to continually expand the repertoire of behaviors a robot can perform reliably in real environments, while improving its ability to learn new skills, adapt to changing conditions, and recover from failure. These practical capabilities provide both measurable outcomes and a foundation for investigating deeper principles of intelligence.




POSITION SUMMARY:

We are seeking a Research Scientist to find how specific fly circuits produce behavior and to turn those mechanisms into models that run on robots. We don't simulate the whole brain. We study modular circuits one at a time. Each project starts with neurons that experiments have linked to a behavior. We then use the connectome to find candidate circuit motifs and to rule out mechanisms the wiring can't support, and we test competing models against neural data, in simulation, and then apply them on physical robots. We welcome applicants from neuroscience, engineering, physics, computer science, and related quantitative fields. This position reports to Chongxi Lai, who leads Astera's Robotics team. 

This is a full-time position.




RESPONSIBILITIES:

 - Choose tractable circuits from the literature. Review experimental studies to find behaviors with strong neuron–behavior evidence, such as recordings, activation or silencing experiments, and behavioral assays. Judge which circuits are ready for mechanistic modeling.

 - Use the connectome to generate and constrain hypotheses. Find the identified neurons in the connectome. Trace their inputs, outputs, and recurrent connections, and pull out candidate circuit motifs. Use the wiring to rule out mechanisms the anatomy can't support, and be clear about what it leaves open, such as synapse sign and strength, neuromodulation, and intrinsic dynamics.

 - Build and compare competing circuit models. Test models against neural recordings, behavioral measurements, and perturbation data to find which mechanisms explain the behavior and which circuit elements are necessary.

 - Test models in closed loop, in simulated fruit fly or robots. Work with robotics researchers to put models into simulated and physical bodies. Measure how behavior changes with sensory cues, body dynamics, noise, and task demands.

 - Make predictions for new fly experiments. Use closed-loop results to refine models and derive quantitative predictions. Work with experimental collaborators to design perturbations that distinguish competing models.

 - Help apply learnt mechanisms to robotics. Turn validated circuit mechanisms into algorithms, or algorithmic principles for robot perception, learning, or control on navigation or manipulation tasks.

 - Build a reusable workflow. Develop shared tools and analysis pipelines so each new circuit goes faster than the last. Share models, code, and findings.




QUALIFICATIONS:

Required

 - PhD or equivalent research experience in neuroscience, computer science, physics, applied mathematics, engineering, or a related quantitative field.

 - Demonstrated experience building mechanistic models of neural circuits that are constrained by, and tested against, experimental data.

 - Ability to read experimental literature critically: weigh the strength of neuron–behavior evidence, interpret recordings and perturbations, and turn them into testable predictions that distinguish competing mechanisms.

 - Ability to make principled modeling choices with incomplete data, such as wiring diagram with approximate synaptic counts but without exact synaptic weights and to state which conclusions depend on those choices.

 - Strong programming and quantitative skills, such as dynamical systems, statistical inference, graph analysis, optimization, or machine learning. Experience building reproducible scientific analyses and simulations.

 - Interest in embodied intelligence and ability to collaborate across neuroscience, AI, and robotics.

Bonus Experience

 - Familiarity with Drosophila neuroanatomy, behavior, or genetic tools. Hands-on experience with connectome datasets (e.g., FlyWire, hemibrain, MANC, BANC), including matching experimentally characterized neurons to reconstructed cells.

 - Experience modeling recurrent dynamics, plasticity, neuromodulation, or sensorimotor feedback.

 - Experience with embodied simulation (e.g., NeuroMechFly, flybody, MuJoCo, IsaacSim), physical robots, robot learning, or control, including models that interact with body mechanics.

 - A record of theoretical predictions that were tested experimentally, ideally with experimental collaborators.




LOCATION:

This position can be based on-site in Emeryville, California (San Francisco Bay Area), or remote anywhere in the US.




COMPENSATION:

This role’s pay range is $120,000 to $180,000, based on experience, skills, and location.

As a nonprofit organization, we're exempt from the H-1B cap; visa sponsorship may be available for qualified roles.




BENEFITS:

 - Top tier health insurance plans with 99% of premiums covered by Astera for employees and dependents

 - Daily lunch that brings the full office together, plus a well-stocked fridge and pantry

 - Licenses for frontier AI tools and software

 - 403(b) retirement plans, flexible paid time off, paid parental leave, commuter benefits, and health and dependent care FSAs




EQUAL OPPORTUNITY EMPLOYMENT & ACCOMMODATIONS

Astera Institute is an equal opportunity employer and is invested in fostering a culture where everyone can thrive. We are committed to equity and inclusion, and we encourage women, people of color, LGBTQIA individuals, people with disabilities, members of ethnic minorities, foreign-born residents, older members of society, and others from minority communities and diverse backgrounds to apply.

Astera Institute is committed to providing reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities in the job application and interview process. If you need an accommodation, please contact us at recruiting@astera.org and we will work with you to meet your needs.
